# Fake Bambu printer (in-process)

Substitutes `FakeBambuAgent` for Bambu's closed network plugin so header menu,
Select Machine, and print can run without hardware. It is not a network fake:
MQTT, FTPS, and discovery are not implemented.

The Klipper/Moonraker simulator lives on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter` under
`tests/printer_sim/` and covers print-host printers. Do not add a Bambu network
fake unless asked.

This file is the operator guide for humans and AI agents.

## What success looks like

- Log: `switch_printer_agent: printer agent switched to jusprin-fake-bambu`
- Log: `set_selected_machine=FAKE001` and later `FakeBambuAgent: connected FAKE001`
- Printer chip shows `Bambu Lab A1 mini · 0.4` (nickname and nozzle only)
- Click the **printer** half of that chip. The **first menu row** is Idle,
  Printing, or Offline. Those words are never on the chip itself.

If the log says `moonraker` or `orca`, the fake is not in the path. Stop and
fix the preset; do not patch UI gates.

## Turn it on

Quit JusPrin first. The app rewrites `JusPrin2.conf` on exit.

`JusPrin2.conf` is JSON. Under the scratch datadir:

```json
"jusprin": { "fake_printer": true }
```

JSON `true` is what the app stores; `get("jusprin", "fake_printer")` reads as
the string `"true"`. An INI `[jusprin]` block is ignored.

Keep a **Bambu Lab printer** selected: a real system preset, typically
`Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle`, or a named printer that inherits one.
`is_bbl_vendor()` must be true; it reads the inherited `printer_model`, so
either works. An embedded 3mf preset named
`Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle(Tape_4_3MF.3mf)` is not enough; the agent stays
`orca`.

**Add a printer…** in the printer menu installs the system preset and saves it
as a named printer (a user profile such as `Bambu Lab A1 mini`), which is what
Home lists. Alternatively copy `Resources/profiles/BBL` into
`<datadir>/system/` and add the A1 mini model to the `models` array in
`JusPrin2.conf`, then select the system preset. Opening
`~/Downloads/Tape_4_3MF.3mf` only helps after that vendor is installed.

Launch a **scratch** `--datadir`. Do not point fake mode at the everyday
config. JusPrin turns `single_instance` on at every start; its instance lock
lives in the data directory, so a scratch `--datadir` runs as its own instance
beside another JusPrin. Do not pass `--no-single-instance`; Boost rejects it.

The fake emulates printer type `N1` (A1 mini). Select Machine lists it as
**JusPrin Fake A1 mini (LAN)**.

For an MCP client, the shell harness does all of this in its own datadir:
`shell_integration_harness --manual-mcp <dir> --fake-printer` saves a
**Fake A1 mini** printer, connects it to the fake and selects it before it
prints `HARNESS MCP FIXTURE READY`. Edits to the conf would not survive: the
fixture rewrites it at startup.

## Drive state

Write `<datadir>/jusprin/fake_printer.json` (create `jusprin/` if needed). The
fake rereads it about once a second.

```json
{"state":"printing","progress":0.4,"nozzle":210,"bed":60,"offline":false}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `state` | `idle`, `heating`/`prepare`, `printing`/`running`, `pause`, `finished`, `failed` |
| `progress` | 0–1, mapped to `mc_percent` |
| `nozzle`, `bed` | °C |
| `offline` | `true` stops `push_status`; after ~30 s the menu first row is Offline |
| `spools` | loaded AMS spools; see below. Absent leaves whatever was last set |
| `send_fails` | `true` makes the next print or storage upload fail as an upload failure (read at the moment of Send), so OrcaSlicer's send dialog shows its error and reports no success |
| `connect_fails` | a code such as `"5"` (or `true`, which is `"5"`) makes every connect report `ConnectStatusFailed` with that code to the app, as the plug-in does for a printer that refuses; upstream reads `"5"` as a wrong access code and erases the saved one. Nothing connects while it is set. Tests can also call `fail_next_connect(code)` on the agent for one connect |

No `spools` (or an empty array) reports no AMS at all, same as before this
field existed. A non-empty array reports one AMS unit (id `"0"`) with one
tray per spool, up to 4:

```json
{"spools": [{"subBrands": "PLA Matte", "trayType": "PLA", "colour": "5F7D4FFF"}]}
```

`subBrands` is what `PrinterDiscovery.cpp` reads back as the spool's name
when set (ahead of `trayType`), so it is the field worth setting for a
saved/network-printer card or receipt to show something. `trayType` is the
spool's material (Home's Loaded row names it); the fake sends it beside a
`tray_info_idx`, since upstream ignores a type that arrives without one.
`filamentId` sets that id (`"GFA01"` is Bambu PLA Matte); left out, the
id is empty, and Orca's filament sync skips the tray. `colour` is optional: a spool without it reports no colour, and Home
draws no swatch for it.

Delete the file, or set `"offline": false` and `"state":"idle"`, to return to Idle.

## Print

Slice, then Print (or Cmd+Shift+G on macOS). Send completes without a printer.
The log records `FakeBambuAgent: start_local_print file=...`.

If the control file is present, that file wins: send still succeeds, but the
menu stays on the file's state. Remove the file if you want the canned printing
scenario after send.

## Isolate a running app (agents)

Another JusPrin may already be open. Do not send keys or clicks to it.

On macOS both processes are often named `OrcaSlicer`. Target by unix pid or by
a unique `CFBundleIdentifier` on a ditto'd `.app` (then ad-hoc `codesign`).
`osascript` `unix id` filters can match the wrong process; prefer
`AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)` or the unique bundle id.

Keyboard events posted to the pid work while the Mac is locked; mouse events
posted that way do not. Menus only open when that app is frontmost. The printer
half of the chip is a wx control (`SetName("Printer")`) and often has no AX
title; click by coordinates after a screenshot, or use the documented shortcut
for Print.

Logs: `<datadir>/log/debug_*.log`. This machine's default `grep` may be ugrep;
use `/usr/bin/grep -a` on app logs.

## A real printer, no model

The printer tools are not exposed over MCP, so `probe.call` cannot reach them.
`shell_integration_harness --printer-network-check <dir> <address> <version>`
drives them with a scripted stand-in for the model, on Bambu's real plug-in:
copy `plugins/` from a data folder that has it into `<dir>` first, and pass the
version in its `libbambu_networking_<version>.dylib` name. It expects a P1S in
cloud mode at `<address>`, prints each tool result and note as
`HARNESS NETWORK` lines, and sends the printer nothing. `--simulate-announce` after
the version hands the app that announcement itself 25 seconds in, for when no
printer is on; it tests everything after the plug-in, not the plug-in. Printers announce on UDP
2021. While another program holds that port the plug-in hears nothing, and
`printer_connection_status` reports `port_taken`, so quit whatever
`lsof -nP -iUDP:2021` names first. The plug-in takes the port only as the app
starts, so once that program lets go the status reports `not_listening` until a
restart. Holding the port from a small script is how to test both states.

`--printer-connect-skill <dir> <address> <version>` runs the same chats for
the connection skill; pass `none` as the version to run without the plug-in.
`--open-issue` after the version also calls `issue_report_open`, which opens
the default browser on a filled-in GitHub issue page. Nothing is filed unless
someone presses Submit there, so close the tab. That run keeps its data
folder; the link is in `log/debug_*.log` under "opening an issue page".

## Unit tests

`jusprin_fake_bambu_tests` (Catch2, GUI build). They cover announce JSON,
control-file parsing, and agent id. They do not start the heartbeat unless the
test sets `set_queue_on_main_fn`.

## Agent id

Registered as `jusprin-fake-bambu`. `GUI_App::switch_printer_agent` uses that
id in place of `bbl` when fake mode is on. No other upstream file is involved.

content.text:
Yes. For OctoPrint and Moonraker printers, Docker simulators running the real software would be cleaner than what we have now. I ran both on your Mac and each one printed through its real API. It isn't quite two containers, though: the Klipper side is three. Bambu printers still need the in-process fake.

**What exists today**
- **Bambu:** `FakeBambuAgent` in [src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md) swaps out Bambu's network plug-in inside the app. You set the printer's state with a small JSON control file. Docker can't replace this, because Bambu's protocol is closed.
- **Moonraker:** `tests/printer_sim/fake_moonraker.py` is a 752-line Python imitation of Moonraker. It only exists on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter`, not on this branch.
- **Docker containers already running:** a session on Nov 3 started `jp-klipper`, `jp-moonraker` and `jp-moonraker-open` by hand. Their configs live in that session's `/tmp` scratchpad, so a reboot will lose them. Their Klipper has no board (`serial: /dev/null-no-board`), so it always reports "error" and can't print. `jp-octoprint` is your own Obico plug-in dev setup, with no printer connected. I didn't touch it.

**What I tested** (in throwaway containers, now removed)
- **OctoPrint:** I used the stock `octoprint/octoprint:minimal` image with its built-in virtual printer turned on and an API key set in advance. It reported "Operational", and a wrong key got 403. I uploaded a file with `print=true`, which is the same form field the app's `OctoPrint.cpp` sends. It printed, and the temperatures climbed. It needed no workarounds and almost no CPU.
- **prind (Klipper):** prind's simulated-board option adds a simulator container, so this side is three containers: simulator, Klipper and Moonraker. Klipper reached "ready". Upload through `/server/files/upload`, then print, pause, cancel and finish all worked. It needed three workarounds:
  - The simulated board reports the X endstop (the limit switch Klipper uses to find zero) as always pressed. So the `G28` homing command at the start of every print fails with "Endstop stepper_x still triggered". I added a `[homing_override]` that just sets the position instead.
  - The temperature reads a fixed 103 °C. So I relaxed the heater safety check and made M109/M190 not wait for temperature.
  - prind's sample config has a 210 °C max, a 0.5 mm nozzle and 3.5 mm filament. Those need changing before it can take real JusPrin G-code.

  The simulator image isn't on any registry, so it has to be built locally once, which took about 6 minutes. It also uses one full CPU core the whole time it runs. A firmware restart can't reset it, so the containers have to be restarted instead.

I didn't point the app itself at either simulator. I only used curl against the same endpoints the app calls.

**Why it's cleaner than the Python fake**
It's the real software, so the auth refusals, error states, websocket and upload behaviour are the real thing, and there's no fake protocol code for us to keep up to date. The cost is precise control. The Python fake could jump straight to "printing at 40%" or "offline". With Docker you get those by sending real commands or by stopping a container. Forcing an upload failure would need extra setup.

**My proposal (not agreed):**
- Check in one compose file that starts the OctoPrint virtual printer, the prind Klipper stack with the workarounds above, and a second Moonraker on the same Klipper that requires an API key.
- Retire `fake_moonraker.py` and the hand-made containers.
- Keep `FakeBambuAgent`.

Sources: [OctoPrint Virtual Printer docs](https://docs.octoprint.org/en/devel/bundledplugins/virtual_printer.html), [OctoPrint virtual printer setup](https://docs.octoprint.org/en/devel/development/virtual_printer.html), [prind](https://github.com/mkuf/prind) (README, simulavr section).

# Print hosts for testing without a printer: a Klipper printer behind two
# Moonrakers (one open, one that wants an API key) and an OctoPrint with its
# built-in virtual printer. All of it is the real software; only the printer
# boards are simulated. See README.md.
name: jusprin-printer-hosts

services:
  # The Klipper printer's board, simulated by simulavr. prind builds this image
  # but does not publish it, so the first `up` builds it (about 6 minutes).
  # VERSION is the Klipper commit of the klipper image below; the board's
  # firmware and Klipper must match.
  simulavr:
    image: jusprin-test-simulavr:0cee841e3
    build:
      context: https://github.com/mkuf/prind.git#6f7690117230f4128101f0b0d2d72bf8a37cae8a:docker/klipper
      target: build-simulavr
      args:
        VERSION: 0cee841e31d701595b3e509a0b502f6e320f52a8
    restart: unless-stopped
    # The simulated serial port is a pty under /dev/pts; Klipper opens it
    # through a link in the shared run volume, so both see the same /dev.
    privileged: true
    volumes:
      - /dev:/dev
      - run:/opt/printer_data/run

  klipper:
    image: mkuf/klipper:v0.13.0-820-g0cee841e3
    restart: unless-stopped
    privileged: true
    depends_on: [simulavr]
    command: >
      -I printer_data/run/klipper.tty
      -a printer_data/run/klipper.sock
      printer_data/config/printer.cfg
      -l printer_data/logs/klippy.log
    volumes:
      - /dev:/dev
      - ./klipper/printer.cfg:/opt/printer_data/config/printer.cfg:ro
      - run:/opt/printer_data/run
      - gcodes:/opt/printer_data/gcodes
      - klipper-logs:/opt/printer_data/logs

      - moonraker-open-db:/opt/printer_data/database

# Klipper printer (MyKlipper 0.4 nozzle: 250 x 250 x 250) so its G-code prints
# here unchanged. Pins follow Klipper's config/sample-simulavr.cfg.

# - Its endstop pins always read as pressed, so homing never finds a switch.

# - Its thermistors read a fixed value (about 103 C), so heaters never reach a
#   target. The heater checks are relaxed and M109/M190 set the target without

# Print hosts without a printer

Docker containers that run the real print-host software, for testing the app's
Moonraker and OctoPrint paths: connecting, API keys, status, and sending a
print. Only the printer boards are simulated. Bambu printers are covered by the
in-process fake instead ([Fake Bambu README](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md)).

| Address | What answers | Key |
|---|---|---|
| `http://127.0.0.1:7130` | Moonraker on Klipper, trusts every address | none |
| `http://127.0.0.1:7131` | the same Klipper through a second Moonraker | needed; HTTP 401 without it |
| `http://127.0.0.1:5030` | OctoPrint 1.11.2 with its bundled virtual printer | needed; HTTP 403 without it |

Klipper's board is simulavr, an AVR simulator running Klipper's own firmware,
set up from [prind](https://github.com/mkuf/prind). OctoPrint's printer is its
[Virtual Printer](https://docs.octoprint.org/en/devel/bundledplugins/virtual_printer.html)
plugin, which acts like a Marlin printer on a serial port.

## Start and stop

Needs Docker (Docker Desktop on macOS and Windows).

```bash
docker compose -f tests/printer_hosts/docker-compose.yml up -d
```

The first start builds the simulavr image, which prind does not publish: about
6 minutes. Klipper reports `ready` some seconds after the containers start:

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:7130/printer/info
```

Print the keys as shell exports (`JP_MOONRAKER_KEY`, `JP_OCTOPRINT_KEY`, and a
wrong one, `JP_BAD_KEY`):

```bash
eval "$(tests/printer_hosts/keys.sh)"
```

OctoPrint's key is fixed in `docker-compose.yml`. Moonraker makes its own key
on first start and keeps it until the volumes are removed. OctoPrint's web page
signs in as `admin` / `jusprin-test`.

```bash
docker compose -f tests/printer_hosts/docker-compose.yml down       # keeps keys and uploaded files
docker compose -f tests/printer_hosts/docker-compose.yml down -v    # back to a first start
```

The simulator uses one CPU core for as long as it runs, so stop the stack when
you are done.

## States worth testing

- **Ready, printing, paused, cancelled, complete:** send G-code with the app,
  or through the API (`/server/files/upload` with `print=true`,
  `/printer/print/pause`, `/printer/print/cancel`). Prints take their real
  time: the app's 20 mm cube on the generic Klipper printer runs about 10
  minutes.
- **Klipper in error behind a working Moonraker:** `docker compose … stop simulavr`.
  Start it again, then restart `klipper` (a `FIRMWARE_RESTART` cannot reset the
  simulated board).
- **Host offline:** stop the Moonraker or OctoPrint container.
- **Nothing listening:** any other port, such as `7139`.
- **Wrong host type:** OctoPrint at `7130` (Moonraker answers OctoPrint's API
  through its `[octoprint_compat]` section, so this connects), or Moonraker at
  `5030` (HTTP 404).

## The printer

`klipper/printer.cfg` matches the app's generic Klipper printer (MyKlipper 0.4
nozzle: 250 × 250 × 250, 0.4 mm nozzle, 1.75 mm filament) and defines the
`PRINT_START` and `PRINT_END` macros its start and end G-code call, so that
printer's G-code prints unchanged. simulavr's endstops always read as pressed
and its thermistors read about 103 °C, so homing sets the position without
moving, and M109/M190 set a temperature without waiting for it. Status reports
the target temperatures, but the measured ones stay near 103 °C.

## With the shell harness

`--print-host-check` takes a file of cases, one per line, and runs the app's
connection tool on each without a model:

```
moonraker http://127.0.0.1:7130
moonraker http://127.0.0.1:7131 JP_MOONRAKER_KEY
octoprint http://127.0.0.1:5030 JP_BAD_KEY
```

Export the keys first, as above.

## Versions

Every image is pinned. The simulavr build's `VERSION` must be the Klipper
commit of the `mkuf/klipper` tag (the part after `-g` in the tag), because
Klipper refuses a board built from different firmware. To move to newer
images, change both together, along with the prind commit in the build
context.

ARG KLIPPER_TAG
FROM mkuf/klipper:${KLIPPER_TAG}-tools

RUN apt update \
 && apt install -y git cmake swig python3-dev python3-setuptools \
 && apt clean

WORKDIR /opt/klipper
COPY config.simulavr .config
RUN make

WORKDIR /opt
RUN mkdir run \
 && groupadd simulavr --gid 1000 \
 && useradd simulavr --uid 1000 --gid simulavr \
 && usermod simulavr --append --groups dialout

 && cd simulavr \
 && git checkout release-1.1.0 \
 && make python \
 && make build \
 && chown -R simulavr:simulavr /opt/simulavr
